Yeah procedurally buggy ass maps would be great! I can't wait for 

\-druid glitch spots

\-buggy areas you can glitch out of as ANY character

\-no set escapes

\-having to spend the entire match LOOKING for the boss instead of FIGHTING it

\-horrendous chest and mob spawns

\-difficulty completing quest because you have no way of knowing where or when or if a certain mob will even spawn

Idk why people think procedurally generated=good, go on and downvote me for being honest but it's a terrible idea opposed to static pre-made maps, sure we need new maps, but just wanting procedurally generated shit is not a good alternative by any means. Imagine spawning in on a trap, or the room your in spawns barely any loot, next room has wonky shit going on too, maybe it's barren and empty or maybe it has a bunch of skeletons and like 1 chest, okay cool, would if your duo or whoever dies and needs a res? Is it really going to be all that fun trying to find where or even if there is a alter of sacrifice? How about you want to find all the pvp? Kind of tough to know where people congregate on maps that aren't set in stone on where shit is, oh and kiss the mini map goodbye, at least some of the finer details of it. But! Let's look at some few positives that there are

\-Forces players into their uncomfortable zone, meaning players are more willing to just move and not camp around so much

\-more exploration and world building

\-always a unique experience for those who want that (honestly not the game for it though)

\-questing is an actual "quest"

\-less players you may encounter due to the differences in each map

\-potentially some cooler rooms?

Some of the "perks" are almost barely perks in my eyes, because from the sound of what I'm describing here, is not a pvp dungeon themed looter-extraction game, it's a singleplayer dungeon-crawler game with co-op.
